text:
maya: FYI customer ACME opened a support escalation — p99 generation latency jumped ~15x after last night's infra patch.
eli: hitting it from prod as well, timestamps attached in the ticket. p95 fine, but p99s are brutal :cry:
maya: ticket #TKT-4821, link: https://support.redwood/t/TKT-4821
maya: reported spike started ~2026-03-15 02:10 UTC, coincides with automatic driver rollout (driver v525 -> v531) in eu-west-1.
liam: ah ok. any repro or stack traces from the serving nodes?
eli: we captured traces and a short flame: kv-cache eviction bursts, then host io stalls. attached fio and perf output.
priya: can you paste the fio summary from one affected node?
eli: "fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=64 --bs=4k --size=2G --runtime=60 --group_reporting" -> iops dropped from 120k -> 14k under mixed load.
ken: that smells like host-side IO qdepth saturation after driver changed NVMe scheduling behavior. Also possible aggressive KV cache eviction increased random reads.
liam: what model serving config? large context models increase KV cache churn. any change in batch sizes?
eli: no batch change client-side. We are using continuous batching on host; cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 56% after the patch.
maya: summary for triage: host IO up, KV cache churn up, driver update around same time. Priority P1 for customer.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0320-1 (auto-escalation)
priya: steps I'm going to run on a repro node: 1) collect nvidia-smi -q; 2) dmesg | tail -n 200; 3) iostat -x 1 10; 4) capture top -o %CPU and iotop. please hold.
liam: also capture /proc/interrupts and nvme smart log: sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
priya: running those now.
priya: dmesg shows repeated: "nvme 0000:65:00.0: queued completion timeout" ~ spikes around 02:12 UTC
ken: good find. queued completion timeout aligns with firmware/driver handshake regressions. can we correlate with firmware versions across fleet?
liam: yes, list firmware across nodes: `for n in /dev/nvme*n; do sudo nvme id-ctrl $n | grep -i firmware; done`
priya: majority are fw 1.3.2, a few older 1.2.9. driver v531 notes mention a timeout change default. suspect interaction.
eli: any short mitigation we can push to customer while we fix infra?
maya: options: 1) temp rollback driver on affected host pool; 2) throttle kv-cache prefetch to reduce IO; 3) route ACME traffic to eu-nonaffected region; 4) bump ephemeral model variant to smaller context.
ken: rolling back is quickest to validate. but rollback has its own risk if other clusters rely on driver features. alternative: set per-pod blkio throttle (systemd/ctr) to cap random read bandwidth from model cache.
liam: can also adjust runtime to favor more in-memory kv-provisioning (increase cache size) to avoid eviction storms, but that requires a restart of the serving process.
maya: customer asked for a short-term fix without downtime.
priya: we can try IO throttling first. I'll apply a soft throttle to the node's service using systemd slice limits: `cat <<EOF | sudo systemd-run --slice=redwood-throttle -p IOReadBandwidthMax=/dev/nvme0n1:200M --scope /usr/bin/bash -c 'sleep 600'` — that caps read bandwidth to 200MB/s for 10m.
ken: test in staging first. if throttling reduces p99 spikes while cache warms, we buy time.
liam: also push a temporary routing rule in the control plane to fallback to model-b for ACME when p99 > 800ms. config change: `routing.policy.acme.p99_threshold=800; routing.policy.acme.fallback=model-b`
maya: action items:
- priya: apply throttling in a staging subset and collect metric deltas (p95, p99, kv hit)
- liam: prepare rollback playbook for driver v525 re-deploy (dry run)
- ken: open CAC card to check firmware-driver compat matrix and escalate to OEM if necessary
- maya: coordinate with customer and offer region failover if needed

priya: applied throttle in test pool, running load harness now.
priya: initial results: p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms, kv-cache hit slowly recovering (+8% in 10m)
eli: can the throttle be applied transparently to prod for just ACME traffic?
liam: yes — we can apply throttling at kube node slice and then tag ACME pods via nodeSelector to schedule on throttled nodes temporarily, or set runtime IO cgroup per pod via cri-tools.
maya: customer accepted temporary throttling to reduce impact. they requested ETA for full fix.
ken: once we confirm rollback is safe, timeline is ~30-60m for a controlled rollback of the driver on affected node pool with rolling restart.
liam: rolling rollback plan: cordon node -> drain -> rollback driver package -> reboot -> smoke test -> uncordon. scripted in `infra/rollbacks/driver-v525-rollback.sh`
priya: will start a small pilot (3 nodes) now, report within 20m.
oncall-bot: Patch rollouts paused for eu-west-1 (automations)
maya: thanks team. keep updates concise here. I'll update TKT-4821 with mitigation and ETA.
eli: thanks all — we're seeing improved tail latencies already. :relieved:
liam: follow-up: will also add a runtime guard to avoid aggressive KV cache eviction in next minor release.
maya: closing loop when rollback or firmware fix is applied. please post final remediation steps and action items for postmortem.
